subject: SDK lifecycle alignment — backward compatibility & major-version timing
messages:
From: Anya Volkov <anya@stellarsync.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partner ask: SDK v2 breaking changes & timeline

Hi Karthik,

Quick note from the StellarSync integrations team — we're evaluating the upcoming SDK changes you mentioned on the roadmap call and a few of our mutual (AcmeCorp) integrations hit real risk if a major-version change removes older client-side hooks.

Two asks: 1) can you share the concrete deprecation timeline for the current SDK surface (specifically: streaming callbacks, request middleware hooks, and the legacy auth header behavior)? 2) would Redwood consider a longer LTS runway for partners with large fleets (we typically ask for 9–12 months)?

Raj from Acme is on copy — he manages the integrations and wants to understand migration effort.

If easier, we can set a short sync — we prefer Tues/Thurs mornings PST.

Thanks,
Anya
Integration Lead, StellarSync
attachments: stellarsync-integration-checklist.docx (see integration inventory)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Anya Volkov <anya@stellarsync.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partner ask: SDK v2 breaking changes & timeline

Anya — thanks for the clear note and for looping Raj in.

Short answer: we want to avoid surprising partners. I’ll pull together a partner-focused deprecation proposal with explicit timelines and migration notes. A few internal items I want aligned on before I share a public timeline:
- exact list of breaking behaviors and the compatible shim story
- recommended migration code snippets and a small compatibility library
- proposed windows for LTS vs. expedited deprecations for deprecated endpoints

Marissa — can you attach the draft proposal and compatibility matrix from the SDK working group? Vanessa/Grace, any platform constraints for an extended 9–12 month LTS for partner accounts (cost or maintenance) we should call out?

Anya — can you confirm whether Raj needs an estimate of dev hours per integration or just a high-level timeline? I can block a 30-min partner sync Tue 2026-06-09 10:00 PDT if that works.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference platform
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft: SDK v2 deprecation proposal (partner copy)

Attached is a partner-friendly draft (redwood-sdk-v2-deprecation-proposal.pdf) and an API compatibility matrix (mvp-api-matrix.xlsx). High-level summary:

- Breaking areas: streaming callback signature (minor change), middleware ordering (behavioral), legacy auth header (deprecated).
- Recommended partner LTS: default 6 months, extended 12 months for strategic partners via opt-in agreement.
- Migration helpers: compatibility shim + sample migration scripts (node/python).
- Rollout plan: alpha for internal + partners (2 months), beta partners (next 3 months), public disable after 12 months.

Costs/ops note: extended LTS requires us to maintain dual-code paths and test matrices for the duration; estimate ~0.6 FTE across SDK and runtime teams during the window unless we supplier automated testing hooks to partners.

I put a proposed message for public docs in the PDF — please review and I’ll iterate.

marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, SDKs
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-sdk-v2-deprecation-proposal.pdf, mvp-api-matrix.xlsx
From: Anya Volkov <anya@stellarsync.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@acmecorp.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: SDK v2 deprecation proposal (partner copy)

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and much appreciated. A few follow-ups from Raj (cc):
- Acme runs the legacy auth header in a dozen places; a compatibility shim would need to be lightweight.
- 6 months is workable, but 12 months is much safer for their rollout (enterprise change windows + procurement approvals).
- We’d like a short migration checklist per major integration type (webhook consumer, async batch, streaming) — can Redwood provide those as part of the partner package?

If you can extend the partner LTS to a baseline 9 months with a path to 12 for named strategic partners, that would probably get us to a signed mutual action plan. We can do Tue 2026-06-09 10:00 PDT for the sync.

Best,
Anya
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Anya Volkov <anya@stellarsync.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, Raj Patel <raj@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: SDK v2 deprecation proposal (partner copy)

Anya / Raj — appreciate the fast feedback and the checklist. We’re prepared to do the following to keep StellarSync and Acme comfortable:

1) Baseline partner LTS = 9 months from publish.
2) Named strategic partners (StellarSync / Acme) will be eligible for an extended 12-month LTS under a short opt-in MOU (I’ll send a one-page agreement).
3) Redwood will publish a partner migration package: compatibility shim, 3 migration checklists (webhook, batch, streaming), and sample scripts.
4) We’ll reserve a weekly 30-min migration office hour for the first 3 months after publish.

I’ll send the MOU and a proposed public message next — Marissa, please update the PDF to reflect the 9/12 month option and include rough engineer-hour estimates per migration type. Vanessa/Grace, flag any constraints on supporting the office hours and extended testing window.

Sync confirmed: Tue 2026-06-09 10:00 PDT. I’ll share calendar invite and the HubSpot link (HS-2026-00432) so we can track the MAP.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the line.

—Karthik
